Type locality. ‘ Niam-Niam; communic. Dom. L. DUDA’. The name Niam- Niam (or Nyam-Nyam) was frequently used by foreigners to refer to the Azande in the 18 th and early 19 th century. The Azande (plural of ‘ Zande’ in the Zande language) are an ethnic group of North Central Africa. They live primarily in the northeastern part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Orientale Province, specifically along the Uele River; Isiro, Dungu, Kisangani and Dorima), in south-central and southwestern part of South Sudan (Central and Western Equatoria States, Yei, Maridi, Yambio and Tombura), and in southeastern Central African Republic (the districts of Rafaï, Bangasu and Obo) (ANONYMUS 2017).
